analysis:
Examined all 11 primary analyses and the replayed metadata/patches. No independently supported regression is established. UpdateRecoveryState.swift:305–319 broadens rollback from a pending candidate to a promoted current release, retaining the predecessor requirement and quarantining the displaced version. SelfUpdater.swift:65 only widens access to an immutable clock closure; AutoUpdateController.swift:127 changes a comment. Documentation describes confirmation, draining, lease-held journaled replacement, artifact verification and cluster/foreground refusals. The replayed CLI patch also resolves the earlier questions about head lines 1852 and 1859–1860: these add command syntax and flag descriptions only. docs/operations/provider-release.md:1033–1044 retains the distinction between local restoration, release deactivation and permanent build revocation.
The combined scope raises T-043/T-013 recovery-integrity and A-018 availability contracts, but local signature validity or offline restoration does not confer serving permission under T-052–T-054/A-017. No supplied change demonstrates altered encryption, token custody, billing, cache isolation (T-041), or privileged fan authority (T-047); hypothetical vulnerable predecessors are not evidence of a regression.
Material uncertainty remains because replay omits 45 of 57 reviewed source units, including executable rollback and test bodies. Further review must directly verify SelfUpdater+Rollback.swift, darkbloom/UpdateRollback.swift and their UpdateSession/ServiceDrain interactions: confirmed-plan and artifact revalidation under the lease, admission/concurrent-start fencing, crash-consistent recovery and quarantine persistence, restart behavior after failure, and fresh connection authorization after restoration. Also reconcile recorded-versus-process version arithmetic for a persistent watchdog after rollback. Prior summaries report checks and tests but cannot substitute for source verification. Missing implementations are coverage limits, not observed missing controls.
